text:
natalie: Heads-up — started a thread after noticing slow mem growth on long-context runs (50k+ tokens) when we fall back to paged KV. Repro on H100 and MI250X but behavior diverges. :thinking_face:
marc: Can you summarize the divergence?
sasha: On H100 we see gradual page churn and a steady PT walk rate; on MI250X there's a sudden spike in evictions and a big tail latency blip.
natalie: Exactly. On H100 the kvcache eviction order stays relatively stable, but unused slot count grows (fragmentation). On MI250X we see aggressive remap+evict cycles — looks like our page table shadowing isn't matching the HW invalidation cadence.
devon: Any kernel or driver differences? ROCm vs CUDA?
tariq: Driver versions: ROCm 5.8.1 on MI250X, CUDA 12.2 on H100. But repro holds across two different MI250X boxes with same driver, so it's not a single flaky node.
natalie: Captured traces with perf counters and our PT debug logs. Key snippet (PT metrics):
```
pt_walks: 1.2M
pt_walk_misses: 340k
page_faults_gpu: 12k
evictions_triggered: 9.8k
remap_ops: 11.2k
shadow_stale_updates: 4.1k
```
marc: shadow_stale_updates stands out. Means our shadow map had stale owner/version entries and we attempted to remap an entry that the GPU still had cached.
sasha: That could explain double-free-style symptoms we saw earlier during migration tests — the GPU kept issuing reads against a slot we thought freed.
devon: How does batching factor in? Could different batching heuristics hide or amplify it?
natalie: Good question. With larger batches we see fewer PT walks per request (amortized), but more simultaneous kv slot holders, which increases the reuse window and therefore the chance of fragmentation coalescing badly. Small batches cause more frequent tiny remaps.
tariq: I ran a quick experiment toggling continuous batching on/off. With continuous batching disabled on MI250X, the sudden eviction spikes reduced but overall throughput dropped 7%. On H100 toggle had much smaller effect.
marc: So MI250X eviction policy is more sensitive to temporal locality skew introduced by batching. Could be DMA coalescing differences or different PCIe/NVLink caching semantics.
sasha: Another datapoint: when we enabled host-staging fallback (we copy hot pages to host and reupload), the MI250X run had a higher page migration latency and more writeback churn. H100 did host-staging faster.
devon: Any stack traces from the runtime when the remap happens?
natalie: Yes — putting a short trace extract: 
```
kv_cache_evict() -> pagetable_remap() -> writeback_async() -> gpu_mem_copy() -> nvlink_submit()
// hot path repeated across threads; each remap correlates with a PT walk miss in logs
```
tariq: I also found a subtle ordering bug in our PT update path on MI250X: we update the shadow map then queue an invalidate, but the invalidate completion callback can race with another thread reading the shadow entry and reusing the slot. On H100 that race is less likely due to faster invalidate completion.
marc: That lines up. We should make PT updates atomic with a version bump visible to readers before queueing invalidates. Alternatively, change the reuse heuristic so recently remapped slots have a short quarantined window.
sasha: Quarantine sounds low-risk. We can add a few-ms hold on reuse when remap count > threshold. That may cost latency but prevent stale-owner reads.
devon: Can we reproduce with a deterministic harness? Maybe inject artificial invalidate delay to simulate slow NVLink.
natalie: I made a small repro harness that toggles invalidate latency; repro rate goes from 2% to 92% when invalidate delay > 6ms on MI250X.
marc: Nice. Can you push the harness and trace output to the thread?
ops-bot: Upload complete: https://redwood-internal/attachments/2876543210/kv-invalidate-harness.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
sasha: Next steps: 1) add short quarantine after remap; 2) make PT shadow update atomic (versioned write); 3) run cross-arch perf matrix (H100, A100, MI250X) with harness.
tariq: I'll own the quarantine patch and run on MI250X lab. devon can handle atomic update refactor.
devon: Ack. I'll add a cheap version counter and a check on readers, avoid heavy locks.
marc: Also add a perf counter for "remap_quarantine_hits" so we can quantify.
natalie: I'll coordinate long-context 100k token run overnight across all boxes and upload logs. If quarantine reduces the spike we should ship an emergency patch to Dedicated for the next release.
sasha: One more thought — kernel selection: maybe our kernel variant that does PT coalescing is suboptimal on ROCm. We should run kernel-level microbenchmarks for PT walk and remap ops too.
marc: Agreed. devon, add microbench harness; let's compare kernel throughput and cacheline behaviors.
tariq: I'll post results here tomorrow. For now flagged as P1 perf/regression candidate. :exclamation:
natalie: Thanks everyone — good thread. We'll consolidate findings into a short runbook after the MI250X runs. :thumbsup:
